 JUDGMENT
[Per Justice Shri U. V. Bakre, President]

 This appeal is directed against the Judgment and Order dated
30/05/2017 passed by the District Consumer Disputes Redressal
Forum, South Goa (the 'Forum' for short) in Consumer Complaint
No. 45/2017. The Appellant was the Complainant and the
respondents were the Opposite Parties ('OPs' for short) in the said
Complaint.
3
2. The Complainant had filed the said Complaint with prayer to
direct the OPs, jointly and severally, to pay to him the compensation
of Rs. 22,999/- along with interest @ 18% p.a. from 01/09/2015 till
final payment.
3. Case of the Complainant, in short, was as follows:
The Complainant had purchased a mobile telephone
manufactured by the OP No.1, from the OP No. 2 through the web
site of OP No. 3 on 14/05/2015 for price of Rs. 22,999/-. The
warranty period of the said mobile phone was from 15/05/2015 to
15/05/2016. The mobile phone was delivered to the Complainant on
15/05/2015. Sometime in the first week of September 2015, when
the Complainant was on a call which he had placed through the said
mobile phone and in the course of his conversation, the phone went
dead. On 04/09/2015 the Complainant took the said mobile phone
to OP No. 4, the authorized service providers for OP No. 1 for
necessary servicing. The Complainant had entrusted the said mobile
phone to OP No. 4 and intimated to them the problem. The OP No. 4
connected the mobile phone to a charger, and realized that the same
was not coming on. The Complainant was told that the phone was
dead and it was handed over to their technician to open it up and
the technician checked it and informed the Complainant that there
was some problem with the main board of the mobile phone and the
battery and that they will have to place an order for the main board
and the battery which would take some time and that the repairs
executed thereafter would be covered under the warranty. The OP
No. 4 prepared a report (Asus Product Service Form) dated
04/09/2015 in which it was written "Waiting for main board and
battery" and kept the mobile phone in aid service centre. However
the Complainant did not receive any call or communication from the
OP No. 4 for some time and hence he placed a call to the All India
Customer Care and explained to the person concerned who
4
answered his call, about the problem faced by him with respect to
his mobile phone. The said person informed the Complainant that
the request to repair the mobile phone, placed by him before OP No.
4 was closed. The Complainant visited the OP No. 4 on 16/09/2015
and the OP No. 4 handed the said mobile phone to him in the same
state that it was in. The Complainant found that the phone was not
repaired and upon questioning them as to why it was not repaired,
he was told by the personnel of OP No. 4 that the water had entered
into the mobile phone and had damaged the main board and the
said damage caused could not be repaired under the warranty and
therefore his case was closed.
4. The Complainant therefore had claimed that there was
manufacturing defect in the said mobile phone and had filed the
Complaint with the prayers as stated above. The Complainant had
produced various documents namely the copy of the legal notice
sent to the OPs with A/D cards, copy of the retail invoice, copy of
the booklet containing the warranty card, and the Asus service
forms.
5. The Forum heard that the Ld. Counsel for the Complainant on
the point of admission and observed that the warranty period was
from 15/05/2015 to 15/05/2016 but the Complaint was filed on
20/04/2016 for which no justification was given. The Forum further
found that the product service form dated 4/09/2015 relied upon by
the Complainant mentioned therein "Action taken mobile returned
to the customer, customer not ready to repair", and that this has not
been disputed by the Complainant in his Complaint. The Forum
held since that the warranty of the said mobile phone expired on
05/06/2016, the Complainant was not willing to get the said mobile
phone repaired by paying the necessary charges and that the same
was evident from the fact that the Complaint was filed almost after
17 months from the time the said phone was collected from the OP
5
No. 4. The Forum held that there was absolutely no deficiency in
service on the part of the OPs and that the delay of 17 months in
filing the Complaint showed malafide intention in filing the
Complaint. The Complaint was dismissed with cost of Rs. 1,000/-.
The Complainant is aggrieved with the above order.
6. Records and proceedings in Complaint No. 45/2017 have been
called for. Mr. Almeida, Ld. Counsel argued on behalf of the
Complainant, Mr. Malkarnekar, Ld. Counsel argued on behalf of the
OP No. 1 and Mr. Salatry, Ld. Counsel argued on behalf of the OPs
Nos. 2 & 3. The OP No. 1 and the OPs No. 2 and 3 have also filed
Written arguments whereas the Lr. Counsel for the Complainant
urged that the appeal memo is itself in the form of written
arguments of the Complainant.
6. We have gone through the entire material on record.
7. It is seen from the records that no notice on the Complaint was
sent to the OPs and thus there was no written version filed by the
OPs. It is not understood as to how merely on the basis of the
product service form dated 04/09/2015, the Forum held that water
had entered the mobile phone. It was not proper for the Forum to
conclude that the Complainant had not disputed the facts
mentioned in the product service form. The Complainant had given
the said Complaint to the OP No. 4, which is the authorized service
centre, within the period of warranty. The Complaint was filed on
20/04/2017. The mobile phone had stopped working in the first
week of September 2015. The mobile phone was returned back to the
Complainant without the same being repaired, on 16/09/2015. Thus
the Complaint was filed within 2 years from the date of the cause of
action and the same was not barred by limitation.
8. The Forum could not have dismissed the Complaint at the
stage of admission itself. The Forum has committed gross error
6
without deciding the matter on merits, after receiving the written
versions of the OPs and the documents on their behalf. The
impugned order is liable to be quashed and set aside.
9. Hence we pass the following:
ORDER
(a). The Appeal is allowed.
(b). The impugned order is quashed and set aside.
(b). The Complaint is admitted and remanded back to the Forum.
(c). The OPs shall file their written version before the Forum within
30 days from the date of appearance before the Forum.
(d). Parties to appear before the Forum on 05/01/2018 at 2.30 p.m.

[Shri. Jagdish G. Prabhudesai] [Justice Shri. U. V. Bakre]
 Member President
